title: The Last Compass Grass
subtitle: Our guide through storms and waves.

items.text: The Last Compass Grass
Bedroom, Suitcase
Strips of palm bark cover the ground. Bundled Compassare, sealed jars of animal oil, and a basket of clean white shells.
A hand-crafted windmill turning in the breeze, a box of pigments ground from scorched reef rock, a Nukutai, and a musician who sails with the tide.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Fatutu, look!
She holds up a piece of tree bark to her face, peeking through two holes like a child discovering something new.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I've found one, too.
Fatutu finds another piece of bark, lifts it in front of her face, and speaks through the cutout mouth hole.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I look like I'm from the forest. Does that mean I'm a ... drueed?
A strange new story, an unfamiliar word, and a clumsy pronunciation.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: You've been reading!

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Selone was teaching me. It's fun to read all the world's stories.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I'm still learning, so I'm not very fast, but they talk about so many things I've never even heard of before.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: You're doing amazing already, Fatutu.
She follows Fatutu's instructions, untying the Compassare and dipping each strand into the oil, one by one.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: This smell is ... It's very special, I must say.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Compassare has many uses. It's a medicinal herb. It helps with stomach pain, inflammation, warts.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Before the ships ever came to Nukutaeao, we often used it to help cure ourselves.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: When we first started trading with outsiders for their medicine, many of the elders didn't trust it. They called it poison.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: They only believed in our island's herbs.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: But Compassare alone can't heal everything.
She learned the importance of having medicine on hand many times over during her sea voyages.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: To the Nukutai, endurance is a virtue. If you get sick at sea, there's no shore to dock at—you can't stop.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: We ride out storms and waves, cast our nets, haul the catch, and return home when they're full. Even if you're hurt, you do your part. When you're back on the island, your kin will heal you.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Have you gone through something like that?

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Yes. We were out at sea, and a lightning storm hit. The whole sky turned blood-red, and the lightning split the waves.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Everyone was soaked. The boat pitched high, and we clung to the rails with all we had so we wouldn't fall overboard.
Barcarola can't help but picture it in vivid detail. She has seen how terrifying a storm could be on the open ocean, but that was in the relative safety of a cruise liner.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I heard lightning strike a crate. It cracked open, and our hala fruits and red snappers rolled into the sea. That was the scariest trip we ever had.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: How did you make it back?

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: We simply shut our eyes and sailed through the storm.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: We put on a charm made from burned Compassare root. It helped keep lightning away.
Barcarola runs her fingers over the root in her hand, its twisted shape soft but dry to the touch.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Before we left, we consulted the Shell's guidance. It told us we'd return safely.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: But the Shell doesn't tell you what will happen, only how it ends.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: When we got back, I looked at the roots. They'd turned to black ash, and the wind had carried them away.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Wow ...

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: I never imagined these leafy things could be so magical.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Compassare ... Compassare ...
She picks one from Barcarola's hand. The dried plant curls slightly, its leaves dulled without water.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: A Compassare's use depends a lot on how it's grown. On Nukutaeao, there are many types.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: The kind we use for Sea Mother's Eyes is the most common. It needs sunlight, so we plant it in bright places. It stores up the sun's light during the day and glows in the dark.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: When we return from sea, the light of these Sea Mother's Eyes leads us back to safety.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: The kind that wards off lightning is planted high up, in a place where it can witness lightning firsthand. That's how it learns to avoid it.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: We climb to the highest cliffs on the island and scatter the seeds there.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: The medicinal kind, well, some we grow by the shoreline, some near fruit trees, and others have to be planted directly in the sea.
She lists the growing methods one by one, but her voice sinks as she continues.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: These ... are the last Compassare.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: The last?

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Yes, the very last from Nukutaeao. After this, we won't plant them again. We won't grow them anymore.
Her hands suddenly tremble as she holds this fading piece of home.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Oh, Fatutu, but are you sure?

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Can we really use these for Sea Mother's Eyes? Just to light up the Trade Fair ... Is that really okay?

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Of course it is.
She smiles, though it doesn't quite reach where it should.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Selone and the other Nukutai—we all agreed already.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Miss Timekeeper, our friends in the suitcase, and the Foundation staff—they've all helped us so much.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: We want to do this. We should do this. Letting these Compassare light the Sea Mother's Eyes once more is a beautiful ending for them.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: If we just leave them tied up in a corner, then they'll just be regular grass—not the Compassare of Nukutaeao.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: But, but ...
She can see her friend is speaking with conviction.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Miss Barcarola, the Sea Mother's Eyes will light up your stage. I'm so very happy about that.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Let's finish these together, okay?

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Just like we did on the boat.
